newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Impoverished Madagascar votes in presidential poll.
newsitem.headline: Impoverished Madagascar votes in presidential poll.

text.p: The people of Madagascar streamed to polling stations in the Indian Ocean island's presidential election on Sunday with a second round run-off looking likely.
Long lines of the most eager among the six million registered voters formed at several polling stations guarded by police in the capital Antananarivo after they opened at 6 a.m. (0300 GMT).
Preachers and pharmacists, admirals and Marxists, aristocrats and traders are all vying to take charge of the world's fourth-largest island, its 14 million people and their chronic poverty.
Joint patrols of police and soldiers took to the streets but maintained a low-key presence with some problems expected at polling stations because of a shortage of cards for registered voters.

With at least five strong candidates out of a total field of 15, political analysts doubt any individual will gain the simple majority to win in Sunday's 12 hours of voting with first results expected on Sunday night.
The early poll was forced when former president Albert Zafy was impeached by parliament for overstepping his powers last July and the constitutional court endorsed the decision in September.
